facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid
No remarkable medical history was noted
A 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on his right upper eyelid
Routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
Revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition
Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
Negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated
